newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia health workers to launch strike.
newsitem.headline: Colombia health workers to launch strike.

text.p: An estimated 85,000 Colombian health workers planned a national strike on Tuesday morning in protest at the government's failure to fulfil a previous pledge on pay, labour leaders said.
There was no word on when health workers' representatives and government ministers would meet to try and avert the strike.

The indefinite stoppage seemed set to paralyse all but emergency medical care in state-run hospitals and health centres across the country. However, health workers' leaders pledged that doctors and nurses would still treat critical cases and provide cover for births.
Health workers' union boss Yesid Camacho told reporters the strike resulted from government failure to meet the terms of a deal to end a nationwide state workers' strike in February.

Under the terms of that accord, state employees were to be granted pay hikes of about 20 percent. But Deputy Health Minister Juan Carlos Giraldo said the government did not have the money to meet the promised pay raise.

Last year the central government deficit ran at more than 4 percent of gross domestic product (GDP). Despite President Ernesto Samper's pledge to rein in the deficit, worker demands for pay raises close to last year's rate of 21.63 inflation have put extra pressure on public finances.
